title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry

source.notes: Facts are paraphrased from Chapter 4 for flashcard and explorer use.

learning_goals: Name substituted cycloalkanes and decide when a ring or chain is the parent.
Recognize cis-trans stereoisomerism caused by restricted ring rotation.
Explain cycloalkane strain in terms of angle, torsional, and steric strain.
Compare conformations of cyclopropane, cyclobutane, cyclopentane, and cyclohexane.
Draw and interpret chair cyclohexane, including axial and equatorial positions.
Use ring flips to connect axial/equatorial positions without changing up/down stereochemistry.
Predict preferred chair conformations for mono- and disubstituted cyclohexanes.
Recognize fused and bridged polycyclic ring systems.

visual_requirements.description: Show skeletal polygon representations of cyclopropane, cyclobutane, cyclopentane, cyclohexane, and common substituted examples.
Display matched ring structures with substituents on the same face or opposite faces and ask for cis/trans classification.
Plot relative cycloalkane strain by ring size and annotate why small, medium, cyclohexane, and large rings differ.
Show cyclopropane, bent cyclobutane, and puckered cyclopentane with Newman-style views for eclipsing or nearly staggered bonds.
Stepwise chair cyclohexane drawing aid with the lower front bond and upper rear bond clearly distinguished.
Overlay axial and equatorial positions on chair cyclohexane, with toggles for top-face and bottom-face positions.
must_show: one axial and one equatorial bond per carbon
axial bonds parallel to ring axis

visual_requirements.description: Animate a cyclohexane ring flip that keeps connectivity and up/down relationships while exchanging axial and equatorial positions.
must_show: end carbons fold in opposite directions
up stays up and down stays down

visual_requirements.description: Compare axial and equatorial monosubstituted cyclohexanes with 1,3-diaxial contacts and A-value style energy penalties.
must_show: larger substituents have larger axial penalties

visual_requirements.description: A 1,2/1,3/1,4 cis-trans grid mapping each relationship to a,a/e,e or a,e/e,a chair possibilities.
Show fused and bridged bicyclic examples, including cis/trans decalin and norbornane, with bridgehead atoms highlighted.

facts.statement: Cycloalkanes are saturated cyclic hydrocarbons.
facts.details: A simple cycloalkane ring is made from CH2 units and has the general formula CnH2n.

facts.statement: The ring is usually the parent when it has at least as many carbons as any attached alkyl group.
facts.details: If a substituent chain has more carbons than the ring, the ring is named as a cycloalkyl substituent on an alkane parent.

facts.statement: Number a substituted cycloalkane to give the first point of difference the lowest possible locant.
facts.details: Choose an attachment carbon as C1, then number around the ring to minimize the locants for the remaining substituents.

facts.statement: Alphabetical order breaks ties when different substituents can receive the same locant set.
facts.details: Ignore multiplicative prefixes such as di- and tri- when applying alphabetical priority.

facts.statement: Halogen substituents are numbered like alkyl substituents in cycloalkane names.
facts.details: A bromo, chloro, fluoro, or iodo group participates in the same lowest-locant and alphabetical tie-break rules.

candidate_cards.front: What is the general formula for a simple cycloalkane?
candidate_cards.back: CnH2n, because the saturated ring is built from CH2 units.

candidate_cards.front: When is a substituted ring named as an alkyl-substituted cycloalkane rather than a cycloalkyl-substituted alkane?
candidate_cards.back: Use the ring as parent when it has the same number of carbons as, or more carbons than, the largest attached chain.

candidate_cards.front: How do you number a cycloalkane with two or more substituents?
candidate_cards.back: Pick an attachment carbon as C1 and number around the ring to give the next substituent the lowest possible number, continuing to the first point of difference.

candidate_cards.front: How is a numbering tie broken for different cycloalkane substituents?
candidate_cards.back: Use alphabetical order of substituent names, ignoring prefixes such as di- and tri-.

candidate_cards.front: Draw 1,3-dibromo-5-methylcyclohexane.
candidate_cards.back: Draw a cyclohexane ring and place bromo groups on C1 and C3 and a methyl group on C5.

facts.statement: Ring bonds cannot freely rotate without breaking the ring.
facts.details: Restricted rotation lets substituted cycloalkanes preserve top-face and bottom-face relationships.

facts.statement: A cis cycloalkane has relevant substituents on the same face of the ring.
facts.details: Both substituents point up or both point down relative to the ring.

facts.statement: A trans cycloalkane has relevant substituents on opposite faces of the ring.
facts.details: One substituent points up and the other points down relative to the ring.

facts.statement: Cis-trans cycloalkanes are stereoisomers.
facts.details: They have the same connectivity but different three-dimensional arrangements.

facts.statement: Common small rings from C3 to C7 are conformationally restricted compared with open-chain alkanes.
facts.details: Very large rings are more flexible, but common small cycloalkanes keep their stereochemical relationships.

candidate_cards.front: What does cis mean for a disubstituted cycloalkane?
candidate_cards.back: The two substituents are on the same face of the ring.

candidate_cards.front: What does trans mean for a disubstituted cycloalkane?
candidate_cards.back: The two substituents are on opposite faces of the ring.

candidate_cards.front: Why are cis- and trans-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane stereoisomers?
candidate_cards.back: They have the same atom connectivity but place the methyl groups on different faces of the ring.

candidate_cards.front: Why does cis-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane not simply rotate into the trans isomer?
candidate_cards.back: Changing cis to trans would require breaking and reforming ring bonds.

candidate_cards.front: Given a cycloalkane with one substituent up and one substituent down, classify the relationship.
candidate_cards.back: The relationship is trans.

facts.statement: Ring strain is extra molecular energy relative to a strain-free reference.
facts.details: Cycloalkane strain can be estimated from heats of combustion per CH2 unit.

facts.statement: Higher heat of combustion indicates a higher-energy molecule.
facts.details: A strained molecule releases more heat when completely burned.

facts.statement: Angle strain comes from bond angles being compressed or expanded away from the tetrahedral value.
facts.details: The ideal sp3 angle is about 109.5 degrees.

facts.statement: Torsional strain comes from eclipsing interactions between bonds on adjacent atoms.
facts.details: Eclipsed C-H bonds in small rings are a major torsional strain source.

facts.statement: Steric strain comes from nonbonded atoms or groups approaching too closely.
facts.details: Steric effects become important in conformational comparisons and medium rings.

facts.statement: Baeyer's flat-ring assumption explains only part of cycloalkane stability.
facts.details: Most cycloalkanes are puckered rather than flat, so torsional and steric strain matter along with angle strain.

facts.statement: Cyclohexane and very large rings are approximately strain-free.
facts.details: Cyclohexane avoids both angle and torsional strain by adopting a chair conformation.

candidate_cards.front: What are the three main contributors to cycloalkane strain?
candidate_cards.back: Angle strain, torsional strain, and steric strain.

candidate_cards.front: What is angle strain?
candidate_cards.back: Energy cost from bond angles being forced away from the preferred tetrahedral angle.

candidate_cards.front: What is torsional strain?
candidate_cards.back: Energy cost from eclipsing interactions between bonds on neighboring atoms.

candidate_cards.front: What is steric strain?
candidate_cards.back: Repulsion that occurs when nonbonded atoms or groups are forced too close together.

candidate_cards.front: Why can heat of combustion be used to estimate cycloalkane strain?
candidate_cards.back: More strained cycloalkanes contain more energy and release more heat when burned.

candidate_cards.front: Why does Baeyer's angle-strain theory fail for many cycloalkanes?
candidate_cards.back: It assumes rings are flat, but most rings pucker into three-dimensional conformations that reduce angle or torsional strain.

facts.statement: Cyclopropane is highly strained because its C-C-C angles are about 60 degrees.
facts.details: It also has eclipsed neighboring C-H bonds.

facts.statement: Cyclopropane uses bent bonds.
facts.details: The bonding orbitals overlap at an angle rather than pointing directly at one another, making the C-C bonds weaker than normal alkane C-C bonds.

facts.statement: Cyclobutane puckers slightly.
facts.details: Puckering increases angle strain somewhat but reduces torsional strain enough to lower the overall energy.

facts.statement: Cyclopentane puckers to relieve torsional strain.
facts.details: A common description has four carbons near one plane and the fifth carbon out of plane, so most neighboring C-H bonds are nearly staggered.

facts.statement: Cyclopropane and cyclobutane have similar total strain energies.
facts.details: The chapter gives about 115 kJ/mol for cyclopropane and about 110 kJ/mol for cyclobutane.

candidate_cards.front: Why is cyclopropane so strained?
candidate_cards.back: It has severe angle strain from 60 degree ring angles plus torsional strain from eclipsed C-H bonds.

candidate_cards.front: What are bent bonds in cyclopropane?
candidate_cards.back: C-C bonds formed by orbitals that overlap at an angle rather than pointing directly toward each other.

candidate_cards.front: Why is cyclobutane slightly folded instead of perfectly square and flat?
candidate_cards.back: Folding trades a little extra angle strain for less torsional strain.

candidate_cards.front: Why does cyclopentane pucker?
candidate_cards.back: A flat cyclopentane would have substantial torsional strain, so puckering makes neighboring C-H bonds more nearly staggered.

facts.statement: Cyclohexane adopts a chair conformation that is essentially strain-free.
facts.details: Its C-C-C angles are close to tetrahedral and neighboring C-H bonds are staggered.

facts.statement: Chair cyclohexane can be drawn from two parallel offset bonds plus one carbon above and one carbon below.
facts.details: The upper and lower end bonds are parallel, and the lower front bond is often emphasized to show perspective.

facts.statement: The twist-boat conformation is higher in energy than the chair.
facts.details: It is nearly free of angle strain but has torsional and steric strain; the chapter gives about 23 kJ/mol above the chair.

facts.statement: Chair cyclohexane is the preferred baseline for conformational analysis of substituted cyclohexanes.
facts.details: Substituent stability is usually evaluated by comparing chair forms.

candidate_cards.front: What is the chair conformation of cyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: A puckered six-membered ring conformation with near-tetrahedral bond angles and staggered neighboring C-H bonds.

candidate_cards.front: Why is chair cyclohexane considered strain-free?
candidate_cards.back: It avoids significant angle strain and torsional strain by keeping bond angles near tetrahedral and adjacent C-H bonds staggered.

candidate_cards.front: What are the key steps for drawing a cyclohexane chair?
candidate_cards.back: Draw two parallel offset bonds, connect one end to a carbon above-right, connect the other end to a carbon below-left, and keep the end bonds parallel.

candidate_cards.front: Why is twist-boat cyclohexane less populated than chair cyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: The twist-boat form has torsional and steric strain and is roughly 23 kJ/mol higher in energy.

sections.title: Axial and Equatorial Bonds in Cyclohexane

facts.statement: Every carbon in chair cyclohexane has one axial and one equatorial bond.
facts.details: Axial and equatorial positions alternate around the top and bottom faces of the chair.

facts.statement: Axial bonds are parallel to the ring axis.
facts.details: They point alternately up and down around the cyclohexane chair.

facts.statement: Equatorial bonds lie around the rough equator of the ring.
facts.details: Each equatorial bond points outward from the ring and is neither purely vertical nor parallel to the ring axis.

facts.statement: Cis/trans and axial/equatorial answer different questions.
facts.details: Cis/trans describes same face versus opposite face; axial/equatorial describes conformation-specific bond direction.

facts.statement: A ring flip exchanges axial and equatorial positions.
facts.details: After a ring flip, axial substituents become equatorial and equatorial substituents become axial.

facts.statement: A ring flip preserves up/down stereochemistry.
facts.details: A substituent that is up remains up after the flip even though its axial/equatorial label changes.

facts.statement: Chair-chair interconversion is rapid at room temperature for simple cyclohexanes.
facts.details: The chapter gives an approximate barrier of 45 kJ/mol.

candidate_cards.front: What is an axial position in chair cyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: A position parallel to the ring axis, pointing alternately up or down around the ring.

candidate_cards.front: What is an equatorial position in chair cyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: A position around the rough equator of the ring, pointing outward rather than parallel to the ring axis.

candidate_cards.front: How many axial and equatorial positions does each chair cyclohexane carbon have?
candidate_cards.back: Each carbon has one axial position and one equatorial position.

candidate_cards.front: Does cis/trans mean the same thing as axial/equatorial in cyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: No. Cis/trans describes same or opposite ring faces; axial/equatorial describes positions in a particular chair conformation.

candidate_cards.front: What happens to axial and equatorial positions during a cyclohexane ring flip?
candidate_cards.back: Axial positions become equatorial and equatorial positions become axial, while up/down stereochemistry is retained.

facts.statement: A monosubstituted cyclohexane is usually more stable with the substituent equatorial.
facts.details: The axial conformation places the substituent near axial hydrogens on carbons three atoms away.

facts.statement: Axial substituents create 1,3-diaxial interactions.
facts.details: For axial methylcyclohexane, the methyl group interacts with two axial hydrogens on the same side of the ring.

facts.statement: The axial penalty for methylcyclohexane is about 7.6 kJ/mol.
facts.details: This corresponds to two gauche-butane-like interactions of about 3.8 kJ/mol each.

facts.statement: About 95 percent of methylcyclohexane molecules have the methyl group equatorial at room temperature.
facts.details: The lower-energy equatorial conformation dominates the equilibrium.

facts.statement: Larger substituents have larger axial penalties.
facts.details: The chapter's table lists small penalties for CN and halogens, moderate penalties for methyl and ethyl, and a large penalty for tert-butyl.

facts.statement: An A-value can be treated as the energy preference for equatorial over axial placement.
facts.details: In this chapter's terms, it corresponds to the axial 1,3-diaxial strain penalty for a substituent.

candidate_cards.front: Which conformation is usually more stable for a monosubstituted cyclohexane: axial or equatorial?
candidate_cards.back: Equatorial, because it avoids the main 1,3-diaxial steric contacts caused by axial placement.

candidate_cards.front: What is a 1,3-diaxial interaction?
candidate_cards.back: A steric interaction between an axial substituent and axial atoms or groups three carbons away on the same face of the cyclohexane ring.

candidate_cards.front: What energy difference favors equatorial methylcyclohexane over axial methylcyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: About 7.6 kJ/mol, roughly two 3.8 kJ/mol gauche-butane-like interactions.

candidate_cards.front: Which has the larger axial penalty in cyclohexane: methyl or tert-butyl?
candidate_cards.back: tert-Butyl; the chapter's table lists about 11.4 kJ/mol for tert-butyl versus 3.8 kJ/mol for methyl.

candidate_cards.front: Why is tert-butylcyclohexane especially strongly biased toward the equatorial conformation?
candidate_cards.back: The tert-butyl group is bulky, so its axial 1,3-diaxial penalty is much larger than that of smaller substituents.

facts.statement: Disubstituted cyclohexane stability depends on both substituents in each chair form.
facts.details: Compare the steric cost of every axial substituent and any additional gauche-like contacts.

facts.statement: cis-1,2-disubstituted cyclohexanes have one axial and one equatorial substituent in each chair.
facts.details: A ring flip swaps which substituent is axial.

facts.statement: trans-1,2-disubstituted cyclohexanes can be diaxial or diequatorial.
facts.details: The diequatorial chair is usually more stable when substituents are not both very small.

facts.statement: cis-1,3-disubstituted cyclohexanes can be diaxial or diequatorial.
facts.details: The diequatorial chair is usually more stable.

facts.statement: trans-1,3-disubstituted cyclohexanes have one axial and one equatorial substituent in each chair.
facts.details: A ring flip swaps which substituent is axial.

facts.statement: cis-1,4-disubstituted cyclohexanes have one axial and one equatorial substituent in each chair.
facts.details: A ring flip swaps which substituent is axial.

facts.statement: trans-1,4-disubstituted cyclohexanes can be diaxial or diequatorial.
facts.details: The diequatorial chair is usually more stable.

facts.statement: The most stable chair usually places the largest substituent equatorial.
facts.details: For unequal substituents, compare A-values or axial penalties to choose the preferred conformer.

candidate_cards.front: Which disubstituted cyclohexane patterns can be diaxial or diequatorial?
candidate_cards.back: 1,2-trans; 1,3-cis; and 1,4-trans.

candidate_cards.front: What axial/equatorial relationship is forced in a 1,2-cis disubstituted cyclohexane chair?
candidate_cards.back: One substituent is axial and the other is equatorial.

candidate_cards.front: What axial/equatorial relationships are possible for 1,2-trans disubstituted cyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: Either both axial or both equatorial.

candidate_cards.front: Which chair is favored for cis-1-tert-butyl-4-chlorocyclohexane?
candidate_cards.back: The chair with tert-butyl equatorial and chlorine axial, because the axial penalty for tert-butyl is much larger than for chlorine.

candidate_cards.front: How do you decide which disubstituted cyclohexane chair is more stable?
candidate_cards.back: Draw both ring-flipped chairs, keep cis/trans stereochemistry fixed, identify axial substituents, and choose the lower total axial penalty.

candidate_cards.front: Why is a cyclohexane-like carbohydrate chair with all substituents equatorial especially stable?
candidate_cards.back: Equatorial substituents avoid the axial 1,3-diaxial interactions that raise conformational energy.

facts.statement: A polycyclic molecule contains two or more rings.
facts.details: Fused rings share a bond and the two atoms at that bond are bridgehead atoms.

facts.statement: Decalin consists of two fused cyclohexane rings.
facts.details: It can exist as cis-decalin or trans-decalin depending on the relationship of the bridgehead hydrogens.

facts.statement: Cis-decalin has bridgehead hydrogens on the same face of the fused ring system.
facts.details: Trans-decalin has the bridgehead hydrogens on opposite faces.

facts.statement: Steroids contain fused ring systems that can be analyzed using cyclohexane conformational principles.
facts.details: The same cis/trans fusion and chair-substituent ideas apply to larger fused-ring frameworks.

facts.statement: Norbornane is bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane.
facts.details: The name encodes seven total carbons and three bridges of 2, 2, and 1 carbon between the bridgeheads.

facts.statement: Norbornane contains a conformationally locked boat-like cyclohexane unit.
facts.details: An extra CH2 bridge connects the relevant carbons and prevents ordinary cyclohexane chair behavior.

candidate_cards.front: What is a polycyclic molecule?
candidate_cards.back: A molecule containing two or more rings.

candidate_cards.front: What is decalin?
candidate_cards.back: A fused bicyclic system made from two cyclohexane rings sharing a bond.

candidate_cards.front: How do you distinguish cis- and trans-decalin?
candidate_cards.back: Compare the bridgehead hydrogens: same face is cis; opposite faces is trans.

candidate_cards.front: What does bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane mean for norbornane?
candidate_cards.back: It is a seven-carbon bicyclic molecule with three bridges containing 2, 2, and 1 carbons between the bridgeheads.

candidate_cards.front: Why do cyclohexane conformational rules matter for steroids?
candidate_cards.back: Steroids contain fused cyclohexane-like rings, so ring fusion and axial/equatorial relationships shape their three-dimensional structures.

integration_notes: This checkout did not contain ochem/data/cards/chapter-02-polarity.json, scripts/build_ochem.py, or ochem/explorer/, so this file is structured as a source record for a future ochem pipeline integration pass.

The existing core deck already had a compact axial/equatorial relationship table; this source expands it with section context, stability reasoning, ring-flip behavior, A-value-style penalties, and visual rendering requirements.

Renderer assets needed before frontend integration include chair cyclohexane diagrams, ring-flip animation frames, cis/trans wedge-dash examples, small-ring conformation models, a strain-energy chart, and fused/bridged polycyclic recognition diagrams.
A-values are represented using the textbook's listed 1,3-diaxial strain penalties for monosubstituted cyclohexanes.
